result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.communicability_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute communicability betweenness centrality for all nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14520-L14653){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.communicability_betweenness_centrality( attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This centrality measure quantifies the contribution of each node to the communicability between all other pairs of nodes. A node with high communicability betweenness is important for information flow in the network. The communicability betweenness of node `r` is: `\omega_r = \frac{1}{C} \sum_{p \neq q, q \neq r} \frac{G_{prq}}{G_{pq}}` where: - `G_{pq} = exp(A)_{pq}` is the communicability between p and q - `G_{prq}` is the decrease in communicability when node r is removed - `C = (n-1)^2 - (n-1)` is a normalization factor ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name to store the centrality as a node attribute. If `None`, defaults to `communicability_betweenness`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return centrality as a dictionary. If `False`, store as node attribute and return self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float] or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: Dictionary mapping node IDs to centrality values. If `return_dict=` is `False`: Self (for method chaining). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or has self-loops. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - values are normalized to be in `[0, 1]` - time complexity: `O(n × n³) = O(n⁴)` due to eigendecomposition for each node - best suited for small to medium graphs (n < `500`) - unlike standard betweenness, considers all walks, not just shortest paths ## Examples {.doc-examples} Basic usage: ::: {#330d6d77 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a simple network graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="B") graph.add_node(label="C") graph.add_node(label="D") graph.add_edge("A", "B") graph.add_edge("B", "C") graph.add_edge("C", "D") cbc = graph.communicability_betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) # Get nodes sorted by communicability betweenness (descending) # Middle nodes B and C have higher betweenness sorted_cbc = { graph.get_label_from_id(nid): val for nid, val in sorted(cbc.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]) } # Returns dict with labels as keys, sorted by centrality sorted_cbc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'C': 0.7156559870110796, 'B': 0.7156559870110791, 'D': 0.0701744795148476, 'A': 0.07017447951484683} ``` ::: ::: Storing the result as a node attribute makes it available for later analysis without recomputing: ::: {#1519daee .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_node(label="1") graph.add_node(label="2") graph.add_node(label="3") graph.add_edge("1", "2") graph.add_edge("2", "3") graph.communicability_betweenness_centrality(attr_name="cbc") graph.get_node_attrs("cbc") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {2: 1.0, 3: 0.14112244211773153, 1: 0.14112244211773142} ``` ::: ::: Compare with standard betweenness: ::: {#1ea4b690 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Star graph star = ec.Graph(directed=False) star.add_node(label="center") for i in range(4): star.add_node(label=f"leaf_{i}") star.add_edge("center", f"leaf_{i}") cbc = star.communicability_betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) # Center node should have highest communicability betweenness center_id = star.get_id_from_label("center") # Returns value close to 1.0 for the center node cbc[center_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: :::
